# Accessibility Conformance Report

<!-- GENERATED by `node tools/check-acr.mjs --write` from `docs/acr/claims.json` — do not
edit. The gate holds every citation below to the repository and rejects a report that
differs from its claims. -->

**Product:** `@pacit/components` 0.0.1 — the Angular component library. The documentation
site and the consuming application are outside this report: a criterion about a page is
theirs, and its row says so.

**Standard:** WCAG 2.2, levels A and AA. EN 301 549, the European standard the EAA points
tenders at, refers web content to the same criteria (clause 9 is WCAG 2.1 AA, which these
tables cover).

**Report date:** 2026-09-05

**Evaluation methods:** the repository's own gates, run on every commit in CI and named per
row — axe-core over every component view and every special state in three engines, a
contrast policy measured on every token build for both themes, a keyboard map tested key by
key per component, forced colours and reduced motion emulated and read back, an accessible
name gate over the sources, and scans over the library's templates and stylesheets for what
a criterion forbids. The assistive-technology pass: **recorded** (see below).

**Status: machine-audited.** The library is built and machine-audited to WCAG 2.2 AA; it does
not call itself conformant until the assistive-technology pass is on record — the wording
law of decision 0061, held by the documentation site's own suite.

## The words

| Level              | What it means in this report                                                                                                    |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Supports           | a gate that runs on every commit measures the criterion and finds nothing wrong                                                 |
| Partially Supports | measured, and a limit is named in the row — an open finding in the plan, or a component card that still owes the reading        |
| Does Not Support   | measured, and found wrong; the finding that owns the repair is named                                                            |
| Not Applicable     | the criterion is about something the library does not ship, and the row says what — where a scan can prove the absence, it does |
| Not Evaluated      | no gate measures the criterion yet, and the row names the finding that will                                                     |

The last word is this report's one deviation from the ITI template, which reserves _Not
Evaluated_ for level AAA. A claim nothing measured is exactly what this document exists to
avoid, so a criterion no gate reaches says so in its own row rather than borrowing a
_Supports_ from a reading of the code; the list of those rows is the work order, not a
footnote.

| **2.2.2** Pause, Stop, Hide                                    | Supports           | Nothing in the library runs unattended past five seconds without a stop beside it. Every face of `[pctHero]` and the button's `hero` variant run ONE pass of four seconds and then stand still, so the criterion's second condition is not met for them at all. The skeleton's sheen is the one that runs for as long as the wait does, and it is meant to: a busy indicator that stopped would say the work had finished, so a cap after N passes was refused outright as the road that lies. What it takes instead is `paused`, an input — the page is the only side that knows how long its own wait has been ([0073](decisions/0073-the-stop-a-long-wait-needs-is-the-pages-to-throw.md)). Three mechanisms, in this order: `prefers-reduced-motion` is the reader's and outranks both — it slows the sheen through the motion axis rather than stopping it, since a still placeholder is the same lie more quietly told; `paused` is the page's; and with neither spoken the motion is the wait itself. The consumer's part is written in the card and not implied: end the wait, or say when it has gone on too long. _Evidence:_ the cards' `prefers-reduced-motion` row: 34 of 34 (20 measured, 14 by argument) · `apps/sandbox-e2e/src/hero.spec.ts` › "the sweep runs its pass and stands still inside five seconds", "`paused` stops the sweep where it stands" · `apps/sandbox-e2e/src/skeleton.spec.ts` › "`paused` freezes the sheen where it stands, and lets it go again", "the stop is one page’s and not the library’s: every other skeleton keeps moving" · `apps/sandbox-e2e/src/preferences.spec.ts` › "the reduction covers every control, not the button alone", "a skeleton’s sheen slows to the loop token and does not stop" · `tools/check-styles.mjs` (point 9) |

| **4.1.2** Name, Role, Value                                    | Partially Supports | Every widget is native where the platform has one and an APG pattern where it has not; the name written on the host reaches the element with the role, states are attributes, and axe's ARIA rules run over every view and every special state in three engines. The one value known wrong — the empty select's listbox — was repaired on 2026-09-06. The screen-reader pass is no longer owed: three readers walked all thirty-six views on 2026-09-15 and 2026-09-16 and every card now carries what was heard. It is not raised, and the reading is why. What the walk answers it answers well — `aria-valuetext` reaches all three readers, a described control speaks its description, a password value is spoken by none. What it does not: a Tab walk never OPENS anything, so a modal, a menu, a popover, a toast, a month grid and a revealed tab panel are unread; a read-only checkbox and a read-only switch are announced plainly checked and on, by both readers that reach them; NVDA announces a radio group and stops; and no reader spoke the chip label that `chip.html` argues is heard beside the remove button. Four findings and one missing pass, all specific: the chip name is 4.70 and the pass that acts is 4.71. _Evidence:_ `tools/check-aria.mjs` (points 1, 2, 3, 4, 8) · `apps/sandbox-e2e/src/a11y.spec.ts` › "the ${path} view has no violations", "the a11y gate really does detect violations (a control of the gate)" · [`req-a11y-built-in`](requirements/a11y.md#req-a11y-built-in) · [`req-a11y-axe`](requirements/a11y.md#req-a11y-axe) · the cards' `Screen-reader log` row: 34 of 34 (34 measured, 0 by argument) · finding 4.70 in [plan.md](plan.md) · finding 4.71 in [plan.md](plan.md)                                                     |

Text alone is enlarged rather than the page zoomed — zoom scales the layout with the text and would measure nothing. _Evidence:_ `apps/sandbox-e2e/src/adaptation.spec.ts` › "text at 200 % cuts nothing off"                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| **1.4.5** Images of Text                            | Not Applicable    | The library ships no image of text: icons are glyph drawings without a `<text>` element, and every word is live text. The gate scans the templates and the drawings for one. _Evidence:_ scan `no-svg-text` — no match in 156 source files                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| **1.4.10** Reflow                                   | Supports          | All thirty-five sandbox views laid out at 320 CSS pixels, one case each, in three engines: the document may not be scrolled on the inline axis at all. Two harness defects and one library one came out of the first run — a column of flex items sized to their own content, a grid track with a 280 px floor, and a field whose automatic minimum was the native input's twenty-character intrinsic width; `pct-field` now carries `min-width: 0` so it shrinks instead of pushing the page sideways. _Evidence:_ `apps/sandbox-e2e/src/adaptation.spec.ts` › "lays out at 320 px with nothing to scroll sideways" · `libs/components/field/src/field.scss` ("min-width: 0;")                                                |
| **1.4.11** Non-text Contrast                        | Supports          | Borders, the focus ring and the states of the controls are `UI` pairs in the same contrast policy as the text, held at 3:1 in both themes on every token build. _Evidence:_ `tools/check-tokens.mjs` (point 7) · `libs/tokens/src/contrast.policy.json` ("UI: focus ring")                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| **1.4.12** Text Spacing                             | Supports          | The criterion's own four declarations — line height 1.5, letter spacing 0.12 em, word spacing 0.16 em, paragraph spacing 2 em — applied with `!important` over everything on the page that holds every component, with no box that clips left holding content outside it. _Evidence:_ `apps/sandbox-e2e/src/adaptation.spec.ts` › "own text spacing cuts nothing off"                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| **1.4.13** Content on Hover or Focus                | Supports          | The tooltip is the only content that appears on hover or on focus, and each of the criterion's three demands is measured: Escape dismisses it and leaves focus where it was, the pointer can travel onto it, and it stays until the pointer or the focus leaves. _Evidence:_ `apps/sandbox-e2e/src/tooltip.spec.ts` › "Escape dismisses it and leaves focus where it was (WCAG 1.4.13)", "the pointer can travel onto the panel and read it", "the leave is waited out rather than cut off"                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| **2.4.5** Multiple Ways                             | Not Applicable    | A page-level criterion about finding pages within a set; the library ships no pages.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| **2.4.6** Headings and Labels                       | Supports          | A dialog is named by its heading, a field by its label, a group by its legend — wired by the library, worded by the consumer; the gate refuses a name written where nothing reads it. _Evidence:_ `tools/check-aria.mjs` (points 2, 3, 4, 5) · `apps/sandbox-e2e/src/a11y.spec.ts` › "an open dialog"                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| **2.4.7** Focus Visible                             | Supports          | One focus ring, one token, drawn with `:focus-visible` by every control that takes focus (a field draws it around its whole row) and measured as a `UI` pair at 3:1 in both themes; under forced colours it is drawn in `Highlight`. _Evidence:_ `tools/check-tokens.mjs` (point 7) · `libs/tokens/src/contrast.policy.json` ("UI: focus ring") · `apps/sandbox-e2e/src/forced-colors.spec.ts` › "the focus ring is drawn in Highlight, not in the border colour" · `libs/components/field/src/text.scss` ("The chrome draws focus around the whole row")                                                                                                                                                                      |
| **2.4.11** Focus Not Obscured (Minimum)             | Supports          | The library keeps one fixed layer on screen — the toast stack, in a corner — and anchors every panel to its trigger. With a standing toast open, every focusable of the view is focused in turn and the element under the middle of its own box is asked for: it is the control itself and not the stack. `elementsFromPoint` and not a rectangle comparison, because a box that overlaps another is not obscured if it is the one in front. _Evidence:_ `apps/sandbox-e2e/src/adaptation.spec.ts` › "a standing toast leaves every control in front of it"                                                                                                                                                                    |
| **2.5.7** Dragging Movements                        | Supports          | The slider is the only dragging there is, and a press on the track or the arrow keys do the same without a drag. _Evidence:_ `apps/sandbox-e2e/src/slider.spec.ts` › "a press lands the drawn thumb where the pointer is, and a drag keeps it there"                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| **2.5.8** Target Size (Minimum)                     | Supports          | A stricter promise than the criterion: 24 × 24 px outright, with no spacing exception, measured per control — the smallest control height is 28 px, and a field's border and affixes are part of its hit area. _Evidence:_ the cards' `Touch target` row: 34 of 34 (22 measured, 12 by argument) · [`req-a11y-touch`](requirements/a11y.md#req-a11y-touch) · `apps/sandbox-e2e/src/field-hitarea.spec.ts` › "a click on the left border padding focuses the field" · `apps/sandbox-e2e/src/size.spec.ts` › "the field and the button at size ${size} have the same height" · [`lesson-14`](lessons.md#lesson-14)                                                                                                               |
| **3.1.2** Language of Parts                         | Not Applicable    | The library renders no text in a language of its own: every string it speaks comes through `PCT_TEXTS`, so a passage in another language cannot come from the library. _Evidence:_ `tools/check-texts.mjs` (points 3, 5) · the cards' `Strings through` row: 34 of 34 (19 measured, 15 by argument)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| **3.2.3** Consistent Navigation                     | Not Applicable    | A criterion across pages; the library ships no navigation of pages.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| **3.2.4** Consistent Identification                 | Not Applicable    | A criterion across pages. Within the library one component is one role and one naming rule, held by the gate; the words are the consumer's. _Evidence:_ `tools/check-aria.mjs` (points 2, 3)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| **3.3.3** Error Suggestion                          | Supports          | The text of the first error is the consumer's own message, delivered where the user reads it; the library adds the channel and takes nothing away. _Evidence:_ `libs/components/core/src/field.ts` ("the text of the first error") · `tools/check-aria.mjs` (points 6, 7)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| **3.3.4** Error Prevention (Legal, Financial, Data) | Not Applicable    | An application-level criterion about legal and financial commitments; the library ships no such flow.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| **3.3.8** Accessible Authentication (Minimum)       | Not Applicable    | An application-level criterion; the library ships no authentication.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| **4.1.3** Status Messages                           | Supports          | A status is announced from where it happens: the toast stack is a `role="log"` and an urgent message a `role="alert"`, the field's error an alert, the select's empty panel a polite announcement, a refused day is said out loud — each measured. The announcer's assertive channel has no caller yet (4.15 in the plan), so nothing rides it. _Evidence:_ `apps/sandbox-e2e/src/toast.spec.ts` › "an urgent message is an alert, and it waits" · `apps/sandbox-e2e/src/select.spec.ts` › "opening it announces the text the application translated" · `apps/sandbox-e2e/src/date.spec.ts` › "a refused day is reached, announced and not takeable" · `tools/check-aria.mjs` (point 7) · decision [0044](decisions/README.md) |

## The assistive-technology pass

**Recorded.** NVDA with Firefox on Windows, VoiceOver with Safari on macOS and Orca with Firefox on Linux over the sandbox views the axe sweep audits (`SBX_ROUTES`, declared in `apps/sandbox-e2e/src/support/views.ts` and imported by the sweep); the logs stand under `docs/acr/at/` (3 files), and every one of the 34 component cards points its `Screen-reader log` row at them.

## What no gate measures yet

Every criterion has a gate behind its row.
